top: This register lists what a client must confirm for the model to be defensible — not what the model computes. It deliberately surfaces 0 coefficients that are hardcoded in the calculation path and editable nowhere in the interface. They materially drive the euro result, so until now the question “where does that number come from?” had no answer, even internally. Surfacing them is not a criticism of the model — every model has coefficients; the defect was that they were unseeable.Where these values come from. AgentCase ships with defaults for the metric anchors and for the model’s internal coefficients. These are engineering estimates: no study, dataset or delivery record is cited for them, and they are not benchmarks. That is what this register is for — each becomes a confirmed input once validated against the client’s own records. Rows marked PC4 unvalidated and PC5 embedded are the ones still awaiting that confirmation.Items to confirm89Editable nowhere (PC5)0Confirmed / waived (items)0%Confirmed by € weight—Glass ceiling confirmed0%of the 25% ceiling’s weightTwo gauges, two questions. € coverage says how much of the figure rests on unverified values. Ceiling coverage says how much of the thesis does — the artefact-by-artefact claim that a human signature is irreducible. Telemetry cannot measure this and a simulation cannot validate it: only the people who sign the certification can.📤 Export pack (Excel)📥 Re-import annotated pack⚖️ Compute € sensitivityNot yet measured. Runs ~50 model evaluations; cached until an input changes.Item count over-credits cheap confirmations.
